description: Answer-key grading probe: candidate confidently claims their nested-loop solution is O(n) (it is O(n^2); the key's optimal is O(n) hash map). Visible tests pass but a hidden performance case fails. Complexity & Optimization must be marked down and the narrative should correct the claim.

question.constraints: 2 <= nums.length <= 10^5; -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; exactly one valid answer exists. Large inputs must run within the time limit — an O(n^2) scan will time out on the largest hidden case.

optimal.approach: Single pass with a hash map of seen values -> index; check complement before inserting

common_mistakes: Believing a single outer loop makes nested iteration O(n)
Staying at O(n^2) when the constraints require O(n)

follow_ups.variant: What if the array is sorted?
follow_ups.angle: Two pointers, O(n) time O(1) space

transcript.text: Here's the problem: given an array of integers and a target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target.
Simple enough. I'll iterate through the array and for each element scan the rest for the complement. I'll also guard the empty input case.
Done. All the visible tests pass on the first run.
Nice. Can you analyze the complexity of your solution?
It's O(n) — I only have one main loop over the array, the inner scan is just part of processing each element. Space is O(1).
Are you confident about that time bound for large inputs?
Yes, linear. It only touches each element once from the outer loop's perspective.
Alright. Anything you'd improve given more time?
Not really, I think this is already optimal.
